subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction and memoryFlush work from foreground same-session message handling, and what transcript-ordering contract should that design preserve?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the repair changes scheduler/session-state semantics across compaction, memoryFlush, transcript rotation, active-run steering, and channel acknowledgments.

options.title: Design a bounded maintenance lane
options.body: Move compaction and memoryFlush to a dedicated bounded or preemptible maintenance path with explicit ordering and recovery tests for foreground channel messages.

options.title: Keep serialization and add visible recovery
options.body: Keep the current same-lane model but add shorter bounded failure handling plus busy/retry feedback so users are not silently blocked.

options.title: Preserve blocking behavior
options.body: Treat compaction as intentionally foreground and defer or close the nonblocking message-handling request as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design a bounded maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Move compaction and memoryFlush to a dedicated bounded or preemptible maintenance path with explicit ordering and recovery tests for foreground channel messages.
